Motion content, § 16-806(c)(1): the motion must state all of the movant's unsealed and unexpunged citations, arrests, charges, and convictions as reasonably known, the grounds for eligibility, and facts in support. The prosecutor is not required to respond. Under § 16-806(d) the motion is served on the prosecutor, but the prosecutor need not respond unless the court orders it. Do not tell users to expect an opposition by default.

Repeat-motion limits: under § 16-806(i)(6), after a denial the court entertains a second motion no sooner than one year, and a third and final motion no sooner than one year after that. A temporary provision, § 16-806(i)(7), exempts motions dismissed between March 1, 2025 and July 14, 2025 from the one-year wait.

Completion of the sentence, § 16-801(2), is unconditional discharge from incarceration, commitment, probation, parole, or supervised release, whichever is latest, and nonpayment of fines, restitution, or other monetary assessments does not prevent completion.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that heard the case for a certified copy of the order of acquittal or dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that heard the case

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look the case up on the iCourt Portal at mycourts.idaho.gov, or ask the court where the case was filed.
